title: Not there, but here: nem before the place

sections.title: Correcting the place
sections.content: To say where you are not going and where you are going instead, put *nem* in front of the place: *Nem a boltba megyek, a parkba megyek.* This is the pattern of unit 11, *Ez nem a konyha, ez a fürdőszoba.* Both places keep the *-ba/-be* ending. Stress falls on the place that *nem* stands in front of.

sections.title: Not this place, that place
rows: I am not going to the shop (but somewhere else).
I am not going to the office (but somewhere else).
He or she is not going to the garden.

items.spanish: Nem a boltba megyek, a parkba megyek.
items.english: I am not going to the shop, I am going to the park.

items.spanish: Anna nem az irodába megy, az iskolába megy.
items.english: Anna is not going to the office, she is going to school.

items.spanish: Ma nem a moziba megyek, a kávézóba megyek.
items.english: Today I am not going to the cinema, I am going to the café.

sections.content: Do not use *nincs* for going. *Anna nincs az irodában* means “Anna is not in the office”; she is simply not there. *Anna nem megy az irodába* means “Anna is not going to the office”. The first is about where someone is, the second about where someone is heading.
